ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended; Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Control Regulations, 2002; Companies Act 71 of 2008, particularly s.56A and s.33(2A) as inserted by General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 1 of 2023; Companies Amendment Act 3 of 2024 (commenced 27 December 2024); Companies Regulations, 2011, as amended; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register (CBOR) filing guidance and the FIC Guidance Notes issued under s.4 of FICA, including Guidance Note 5 on beneficial ownership and Guidance Note 7 on politically exposed persons.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each non-resident beneficial owner's passport identification page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public in the owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State or U.K. FCDO Legalisation Office); accepted by CIPC, SARS, and South African banks

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each non-resident shareholder or beneficial owner (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility service provider or account-holding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille; full consular legalization at a South African embassy or high commission where the country of origin is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, memorandum and articles, and certificate of good standing of any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; non-Hague jurisdictions require full consular legalization by the South African diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking relationship, source of funds, and absence of adverse conduct for each funding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding financial institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the bank officer's signature followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed acceptance of office as first director and consent to act (delivered to CIPC on incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African Commissioner of Oaths for local directors; notary public in the director's jurisdiction for foreign-based directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic sworn declaration for South African directors; foreign originals require Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior management by the instructing accountable institution (law firm or registered auditor) against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the South African list of terrorist and related entities published in the Government Gazette by the Director-General of the Department of Home Affairs under s.25 of FICA; (iii) the OFAC SDN List where USD payment rails or U.S. app store payouts are used; (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists where EU or UK payment rails are used; (v) FATF statements on high-risk jurisdictions and the FATF increased-monitoring list, noting that South Africa was removed from the FATF grey list at the October 2025 plenary; and (vi) politically exposed persons identification under FIC Guidance Note 7, including domestic prominent positions, family members, and close associates. Any PEP or sanctions match triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and, where applicable, a suspicious transaction report to the Financial Intelligence Centre. Screening results must be evidenced, retained for at least five years, and refreshed before any material dividend or share-transfer event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services portal operated by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - https://eservices.cipc.co.za; name reservation is governed by s.11 and s.12 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Companies Regulations, 2011
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must appear in Latin (Roman) script and may be expressed in any one or more of the eleven official South African languages; no transliteration is required for English or Afrikaans names. The legal-form suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd' is mandatory. The name must not be the same as or confusingly similar to an existing or protected company name, must not contain offensive words, and must not falsely imply an association with the South African State, a minister, a municipality, a foreign government, or any regulated profession.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC refuses a proposed name, the applicant may: (1) re-file a corrected application with alternative names through CIPC e-Services; (2) submit a written reconsideration request to CIPC explaining why the name is not prohibited or confusingly similar; (3) where a third-party right is disputed, apply to the Companies Tribunal under s.160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Companies Tribunal Regulations, 2011 for a determination, which is decided on the papers within a prescribed period; (4) request an extension of an already-reserved name before expiry by filing the prescribed e-Services application, with CIPC retaining discretion to extend for a further period in exceptional circumstances; and (5) pursue a High Court review of any adverse Companies Tribunal determination. Professional legal submission support should be engaged at the reconsideration stage to preserve appeal rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally permissible for a software and MMORPG publishing company. Section 23(3)(a) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requires a registered office address within South Africa capable of receiving and acknowledging service of process during business hours; a post office box or mail-forwarding address alone is prohibited. A licensed virtual-office or co-working provider that maintains a physical presence, exercises supervision, and accepts service of process on behalf of the company satisfies the statutory requirement. The same physical address and operational control are relevant for SARS correspondence and tax-residence analysis, although a South African-incorporated company is a per-se tax resident under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 irrespective of the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5%, during the first 12 months for a standard private company in ISIC 5820 with no financial-services or gambling license; the risk rises to approximately 15-20% if SARS initiates a VAT or income-tax audit, if CIPC conducts a beneficial-ownership verification under s.56A of the Companies Act, or if the FIC issues an AML/CFT examination notice. Unannounced physical visits are more probable for companies using residential addresses or mismatched virtual-office records, so the registered office must match all CIPC, SARS, and bank filings precisely.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name reservation fee for one primary and one alternative proposed name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC statutory tariff of ZAR 50 per name, converted at approximately 18.2 ZAR/USD

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; sections 13–19 (incorporation and legal personality), 31 (solvency and liquidity test), 40–41 (consideration for shares), 66–67 (board of directors); Companies Regulations, 2011 (regulations 12–18); Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 (section 228, public officer).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), e-Services portal (www.cipc.co.za)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1) and directors' written consents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no statutory escrow account apply to a South African private company (Pty) Ltd; the Companies Act 71 of 2008 abolishes par value and authorised capital. Shares are issued under sections 40–41 subject to the board's solvency-and-liquidity determination under section 31. Foreign founders may hold 100% of the issued shares without exchange-control approval, provided subscription consideration is settled through an Authorised Dealer (commercial bank) and the beneficial ownership declaration is filed with CIPC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This First Board Resolution of the Company is adopted in duplicate on [date]. RESOLVED THAT: 1. the incorporation of the Company as a private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 is ratified, including the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission; 2. the allotment and issue of 1,000 ordinary shares to the founding subscribers is approved as fully paid; 3. the registered office at [physical address], Republic of South Africa, is adopted as the statutory seat; 4. [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed first directors, holding office until the first annual general meeting, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; 5. the directors are authorised to open the Company's bank accounts, register with SARS, the Compensation Fund and UIF, and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Memorandum of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search on the CIPC e-Services portal to verify availability of the proposed company name and one or two alternate names. Submit the prescribed name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1) online, pay the prescribed fee, and simultaneously draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008, adopting the standard MOI or a tailored MOI that specifies the company's principal business, director powers, and share class structure. Retain the reserved name number for use in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of a Company Name)
Certified ID or passport copies of all founding shareholders and directors
Draft Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1)
Proof of name reservation payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh reservation with a distinctly different mark, or proceed to incorporate using the company registration number as the name. If a third party lodges a name objection, respond via the CIPC prescribed objection procedure within 20 business days; alternatively abandon the disputed name and incorporate under a reserved alternate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Notice of Incorporation and MOI to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation online by uploading the completed Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), the MOI (Form CoR 15.1) executed by each incorporator, and the directors' written consents to act. Attach certified copies of identity documents and proof of the registered office address. An authorised representative or registered CIPC agent must authenticate the submission; the statutory filing fee is payable electronically. For a standard private company, the streamlined incorporation route may be used.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Form CoR 15.1 (Memorandum of Incorporation)
Directors' written consents to act (each director)
Certified copies of directors' and incorporators' ID/passports
Proof of registered office address (lease or municipality utilities statement)
Beneficial ownership schedule and declaration (CIPC form CoR 44.1), if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a defect or query notice, correct the identified particulars and resubmit electronically within 5 business days of the notice. If the filing is rejected, pay the resubmission fee and re-file with the corrected documents; escalation to the CIPC call centre or a registered company service provider is available to resolve material backlogs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services, Company Records and Certificates Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) from the CIPC e-Services portal and verify the company registration number, date of incorporation, and registered name. Prepare and execute share certificates reflecting the 1,000 issued ordinary shares. Establish the securities register, directors' register, and beneficial ownership register required by section 25 of the Companies Act and regulation 16 of the Companies Regulations, 2011, and maintain these registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.3 (Certificate of Incorporation)
Directors' written consent and declaration forms
Share certificates and shareholders' register
Beneficial ownership register (CIPC form CoR 44.2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains incorrect particulars, apply to CIPC for rectification under section 14 of the Companies Act with a supporting affidavit and the prescribed correction form; CIPC will issue a corrected certificate. Late or inaccurate beneficial ownership filings may attract administrative penalties and should be remedied by voluntary filing before the annual return date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax, Unemployment Insurance, and Compensation Fund Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour (UIF and Compensation Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: CIPC automatically transmits the company's registration details to SARS, but the company must complete its income tax profile and register as an employer on SARS eFiling. Register for Value-Added Tax if taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1 million per 12 months, or voluntarily where appropriate. Register as an employer for PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy using the EMP101 form, and register the company with the Compensation Fund under COIDA using form W.As. 2 to obtain a letter of good standing. Appoint a public officer in terms of section 228 of the Tax Administration Act for all SARS correspondence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
Directors' identity documents and SARS income tax numbers
SARS VAT 101 and EMP101 registration forms
COIDA registration form (W.As. 2)
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS income tax registration is not reflected within 10 business days, request a manual SARS activation by visiting the SARS branch with the incorporation certificate and MOI. If VAT clearance or registration is delayed, escalate via the SARS 'Stage 2' complaint channel or appointed tax practitioner. For Compensation Fund letter of good standing delays, escalate to the Provincial Compensation Commissioner with proof of submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Post-Incorporation Governance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks operating under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001; CIPC for annual maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account at a South African commercial bank after completing Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) customer due diligence, including submission of beneficial ownership declarations. Pass a banking resolution authorising signatories. Thereafter, on an ongoing basis, file the company's annual return and beneficial ownership declaration with CIPC on each anniversary of incorporation, appoint an auditor or registered accounting officer in accordance with the public interest score thresholds, and hold annual general meetings as required by the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
First board resolution authorising bank account opening and signatories
FICA customer due diligence and beneficial ownership declaration forms
Proof of identity and source of funds for shareholders
Company business profile and projected transaction volumes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank queries the corporate structure or beneficial ownership information, supplement the application with a group structure chart, resolution, and notarised identity documents. If CIPC imposes penalties for late annual return filing, file promptly and apply for penalty remission under section 26 of the Companies Act; if the accounting officer appointment is impossible, obtain a public interest score assessment and appoint a registered auditor before year-end.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Film and Publication Board of South Africa (FPB) for content classification; no industrial or manufacturing licensing authority applies to ISIC 5820 software publishing because the business is purely digital and does not operate a factory or physical production plant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Film and Publication Board Classification Certificate for the Distribution of a Video Game (Hardcore MMORPG) under the Films and Publications Act 65 of 1996, as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3: office-based IT software publisher; no listed activity under the EIA Regulations, 2014 (Listing Notices 1–3) triggers a Basic Assessment or Scoping and Environmental Impact Report. Electronic waste generated from office IT hardware is regulated under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge applies; sanitary wastewater must conform to municipal sewer bylaws. If backup diesel generators or server racks are installed, air emissions must comply with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 threshold for Low-Risk generators, and noise control must meet SANS 10103 limits. All e-waste must be consigned to a registered recycling facility in accordance with the Waste Information Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and certificate of occupancy from the local municipality under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400); Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance, including an electrical certificate of compliance (COC), first-aid equipment, evacuation plans, and a workplace inspection by the Department of Employment and Labour; COIDA registration letter of good standing from the Compensation Fund covering all employees; general fire safety clearance and structural load inspection for the leased office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; Lehae la SARS, 299 Bronkhorst Street, Pretoria.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) under Companies Act 71 of 2008; CIPC issues the enterprise number and shares particulars with SARS. 2) SARS automatically registers the domestic company for income tax and issues an income tax reference number. 3) Compulsory VAT registration is effected via eFiling (Form VAT101) within 21 days of exceeding the ZAR 1,000,000 taxable-supply threshold in the preceding 12 months or where such exceedance is expected in the next 12 months (Section 23(1), VAT Act 89 of 1991); voluntary registration is available at the ZAR 50,000 threshold (Section 23(3)). 4) On employing staff, register for PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy. 5) Appoint a public officer resident in South Africa within one month of commencing business (Section 246, Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011). 6) Foreign shareholders may hold 100% of the (Pty) Ltd with no exchange-control approval required for equity capital, subject to ordinary reporting through an authorised dealer. 7) Obtain and maintain a SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) pin for imports, tenders, and regulatory licences.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A South African (Pty) Ltd is a separate taxpayer taxed on worldwide income at the current corporate income tax rate of 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023); residence is determined by incorporation or effective management in South Africa. No pass-through treatment is available for a (Pty) Ltd.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; legal form is determinative and a (Pty) Ltd is a company per se. Available elections and mandatory regimes include: (a) Small Business Corporation status under Section 12E (progressive corporate rates where all shareholders are natural persons and gross income does not exceed the statutory cap); (b) Section 11D research and development super-deduction (150% expenditure deduction, subject to advance SARS approval); (c) voluntary VAT grouping under Section 50 of the VAT Act for closely linked persons; (d) voluntary VAT registration at the ZAR 50,000 threshold under Section 23(3) of the VAT Act; (e) hybrid debt and hybrid mismatch rules under Sections 8E, 8F, 8FA, and 23M–23N are mandatory and may not be elected out of; (f) controlled foreign company rules under Section 9D apply where the (Pty) Ltd holds interests in non-South African subsidiaries, with certain active-business exemptions claimable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) – Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration for taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months or where expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in the next 12 months); voluntary registration threshold is ZAR 50,000 (Section 23(3), VAT Act). Foreign suppliers of electronic services to South African residents are required to register for VAT irrespective of turnover with effect from 1 April 2019.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance authorisation regime currently applies. SARS has adopted a phased e-invoicing framework aligned with the PEPPOL 4-corner model (pilot commenced August 2023; mandatory adoption is being phased by taxpayer segment and is not yet universally effective). Vendors must issue Section 20(4)-compliant VAT invoices (full tax invoice where consideration exceeds ZAR 5,000; abridged invoice at or below ZAR 5,000) and file VAT200/VAT201 returns electronically via eFiling or SARS-certified API solutions. SARS performs risk-based data matching, including cross-matching app store payout data, banking transactions, and VAT returns, but does not require an invoice-level clearance code before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported services applies under Section 11(2)(k) of the VAT Act where services are supplied to a non-resident who is not present in South Africa at the time the services are rendered, and under Section 11(2)(l) where services are physically rendered wholly or partly outside South Africa; in both cases the supply must not be directly connected with land or movable property situated in South Africa. For the hardcore MMORPG global model, in-app purchases, subscriptions, and virtual access supplied to non-resident end-users and/or remitted through Apple App Store or Google Play (as non-resident sellers of record or intermediaries) qualify for zero-rating, whereas supplies to South African resident end-users attract VAT at 15%. The supplier must obtain and retain sufficient documentary evidence of the non-resident status of the recipient and offshore enjoyment of the service; inadequate substantiation results in VAT at 15% being assessed on the supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed service or distribution agreement with the non-resident app store operator (Apple App Store / Google Play) or direct non-resident end-customer contract
Section 20(4)-compliant VAT invoice issued by the (Pty) Ltd clearly indicating the zero-rated nature of the supply

Foreign-currency inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103 or Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an authorised dealer bank; where consolidated platform payouts are received, the app store payout statement serves as the supporting reconciliation
App store payout statements and platform transaction-level analytics evidencing purchaser country, user ID, and supply to non-residents
Residency evidence of the counterparty where available (e.g., foreign VAT registration number, certificate of residence, or public company registry extract)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS operates a dedicated VAT Business Unit and a cross-border digital economy audit programme that cross-matches app store payout data, bank statements, and VAT201 filings. If zero-rating is unsupported, misapplied, or accompanied by fraudulent documentation: (i) the full 15% VAT is retrospectively clawed back under an additional assessment within the extended prescription period of 5 years, or 10 years for material non-disclosure (Section 99, Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011); (ii) understatement penalties under Section 222/223 TAA are imposed at graduated rates of 10% (substantial understatement), 25% (failure to exercise reasonable care), 50% (no reasonable grounds for tax position), or 150% (intentional tax evasion); (iii) a late- or non-payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding amount plus interest at the SARS prescribed rate is added; (iv) failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days breaches exchange-control rules under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, attracting administrative penalties and possible forfeiture or Suspension of the TCS status; and (v) deliberate evasion may result in criminal prosecution under Section 234 TAA (fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years) and personal liability of directors under Section 19 of the VAT Act where VAT was deducted or collected but not accounted for to SARS.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated in terms of the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible on the current account, including software licensing and game publishing royalties, with payments routed through an authorised dealer. On the capital account, non-resident inward equity investment in a South African private company does not require prior SARB approval if reported through an authorised dealer and funded through normal banking channels; no mandatory inward listing is required for a standard Profit/Risk-taking (Pty) Ltd. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders, primarily dividends, is permissible through an authorised dealer without SARB pre-approval provided the underlying capital was lawfully introduced, the remittance is matchable to distributable reserves, SARS tax clearance is in order, and applicable dividend withholding tax has been administered. Hurdles are documentary rather than structural: shareholder resolutions, proof of foreign direct investment declaration, audited or reviewed financial statements, and SWIFT source documentation must be preserved for FinSurv audits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Africa operates a floating exchange rate and does not impose a mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; however, all export receipts must be surrendered into the South African banking system through an authorised dealer in ZAR. Payment for exported goods or services must be received within 180 days from the date of shipment or provision of service, or any extended period approved by the authorised dealer and FinSurv. The full proceeds must be credited to the exporter's ZAR account with an authorised dealer, evidenced by Form B/ECS documentation. For digital publishing, Apple App Store and Google Play payouts routed as contractual service proceeds qualify as export revenue and must be received in the same manner, with applicable VAT and corporate tax obligations discharged before onward treasury deployment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Business Current Account / Capital Equity Escrow Account
Premium Business Account / Non-Resident Direct Investment Equity Account
Business Suite Transactional Account / Inward Capital Escrow Account
Relationship Banking Operational Account / Equity Investment Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury and settlement infrastructure. Offshore digital EMI/neobanking providers are not licensed as banks by SARB and cannot independently offer ZAR settlement capability, participate in SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement), or provide a fully regulated receiving account for Apple App Store and Google Play payouts. Their use should be limited to supplementary virtual-card spend and foreign-currency management under an authorised dealer relationship; all primary inbound capital, operational receipts, and outbound trade settlements must stay within the licensed South African banking system to comply with the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act, the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, and Exchange Control Regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2002 (FICA) requires accountable institutions to verify both the entity and its natural-person beneficial owners, directors, and signatories before account activation. A physical visit is not a categorical statutory mandate; SARB and FICA permit remote onboarding using electronic verification, independent contact with the relevant director, notarised corporate documents, video interviews, and third-party database checks. In practice, tier-one South African banks generally require at least one principal director or senior manager to attend a physical verification session at a South African branch, or at an accredited foreign representative office, for medium-risk international corporate clients. Where physical attendance is waived, the client accepts enhanced due diligence, remote video identification, apostilled company documents, and a notarised board resolution authorising the account relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: foreign shareholders behind a chain of offshore holding entities obscure the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC company extracts and share register; signed declarations of beneficial ownership (FICA section 21B-compliant); constitutional documents and shareholders' agreement; notarised passports and proof of residential address for all natural persons above the 10% threshold; a clear chart of ownership from ultimate beneficial owners through each intermediary entity; and a resolution from the South African board confirming the UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and wealth cannot be tied to identifiable value creation, particularly where early-stage capital comes from crypto assets or unregulated foreign gaming wallets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 or MT202 callback records for every inward remittance; bank and custody statements from the entity and its direct shareholders for a minimum of 6 to 12 months; audited or independently reviewed financial statements; shareholder loan agreements or subscription agreements with proper valuation support; and narrative evidence of trading history or prior profitable gaming operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment descriptors or unexplained transaction velocity: in-app purchase payouts from Apple/Google, large royalty payments, or frequent refunds and chargebacks may trigger fraud and sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Apple App Store and Google Play payout reports; platform settlement statements reconciling app store fees, refunds, chargebacks, and value-added tax; written refund and fraud management policies; API-level transaction logs or management summaries; and an anti-money-laundering/terrorist financing risk assessment showing the MMORPG's Low_Risk_Standard rating.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential tax-non-residence or permanent-establishment concern triggered by remote directors, foreign domiciliation, or an offshore treasury committee mandating South African bank accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS tax compliance status PIN; board minutes confirming strategic management is exercised in South Africa; management accounts and payroll evidence; foreign director self-certifications of tax residence (CRS declaration and US IRS Form W-8 or W-9 as applicable); and a legal opinion that the central administration and economic substance of the entity are located in South Africa.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must remit equity subscription proceeds in a permitted foreign currency or ZAR from a non-resident designated account through an authorised dealer. The compliant SWIFT protocol is an MT103/MT202 from the shareholder's licensed bank, with the beneficiary bank being the South African account-holding authorised dealer, the beneficiary account matched exactly to the company's registered entity name, and remittance information indicating an inward direct investment in equity. The remittance should be designated as foreign direct investment (FDI) for Balance of Payments reporting, not as a trade invoice; the authorised dealer completes the inward BOP declaration and any Form/ECS requirement. Supporting evidence is the board resolution approving the share allotment, the subscription agreement, proof of banking source in the foreign jurisdiction, and immediate entry into the CIPC-issued share register and SARB financial surplus declaration where required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for external trade, software licensing, cloud infrastructure, marketing, and international vendors are routed through (i) domestic ZAR RTGS via SAMOS for local transaction parties, (ii) SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border vendor wire transfers, and (iii) International Commercial Letter of Credit (Documentary Credit) where the transaction demands bank-intermediated trade payment protection. For every outward remittance above low-value thresholds, the company must obtain an authorised dealer foreign-exchange approval, present the underlying contract, invoice, licence agreement, or purchase order, and produce a SARS tax compliance and tax withholding analysis where royalties or service fees are involved. All outward payments must be captured under the correct BOP service or trade code and supported by documentation proving genuine business purpose; no advance payment or deferred settlement may be used to circumvent exchange-control limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) transacted with a SARB authorised dealer, fully covered by an identified underlying foreign-currency exposure such as anticipated USD payouts from Apple and Google.
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS or CIRS) used for long-term foreign-currency liabilities, including shareholder loans or international funding related to global game distribution and infrastructure.
Currency Swaps and FX Swaps with a licensed authorised dealer, limited to non-speculative hedging of committed treasury exposures.

FX Option and zero-cost collar structures with a South African authorised dealer where the underlying foreign-currency cash flow is evidenced and the structure does not create synthetic foreign financing contrary to Exchange Control Regulations.
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) limited to documented offshore hedging needs with a licensed non-resident counterparty and prior FinSurv approval where required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately ZAR 125 per month; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers a CIPC compliance notice and administrative deregistration under section 82 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) Filing / Independent Review Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (if required by Public Interest Score) or shareholders/memorandum of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end if compulsory under the Companies Act or the MOI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC compliance notice may be issued; directors may be held personally liable for failure to prepare and present financial statements within the prescribed period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the company's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of unpaid tax plus interest; understatement penalty of up to 20% for non-disclosure under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (embedded in CIPC Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as annual return deadline; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 15 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC may impose administrative penalties up to ZAR 500 per day for non-compliance; failure to update beneficial ownership is an offence under the Companies Act and may restrict future transactional filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for public companies, state-owned companies, or any company with a Public Interest Score (PIS) of 350 or more; PIS of 100-349 requires an independent review; PIS below 100 may be self-reviewed unless the Memorandum of Incorporation requires otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for public interest entities; IFRS for SMEs for non-public interest companies; conformity with the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every private company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) at its registered office; BOR data must be confirmed or updated annually as part of the CIPC annual return; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the BOR and filed with CIPC within 15 business days; failure to do so is a statutory offence.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.00% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. The most relevant preferential deduction is the section 11D R&D incentive: an additional 50% deduction (150% total) for approved qualifying research and development expenditure. Game software development may qualify only where it creates new knowledge, is approved by the Department of Science and Innovation, and is undertaken in South Africa. Additional deductions include the section 12H learnership allowance and certain section 12B allowances for renewable-energy assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Company Income Tax Return; submitted exclusively through the SARS eFiling system by the company or an authorised tax practitioner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The year of assessment runs for 12 months ending on the last day of the company's elected financial year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year. For a company with a 28 February year-end, the ITR14 deadline is the following 28 February; SARS may grant an extension only on application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company's SARS tax reference number, registered name, registration number, financial year end, and the applicable tax type 'Company'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The South African (Pty) Ltd must be identified as the taxpayer. Non-resident shareholders and directors are not entered unless they have a separate South African tax registration or a representative office creating a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A, Box 2 – Principal Business Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the applicable standard industrial classification. For the MMORPG business, use ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210 and describe the commercial model as 'Software Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games with in-app purchases'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the South African entity's business activity. Income of non-resident platform entities is reportable in South Africa only if attributable to a South African PE or if the non-resident has South African-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 3 – Gross Income / Turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare total gross receipts before deductions, including global payout proceeds from Apple App Store and Google Play attributable to the South African entity, less any distribution commissions only if properly structured and supported.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot allocate their foreign platform revenue to the South African entity merely to reduce tax. The gross income field should reflect the South African company's own revenue, after applying arm's-length intercompany arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List income exempt from normal tax, such as exempt dividends received or foreign branch income if a specific exemption applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: South African-source digital gaming revenue is not exempt. Non-resident shareholders cannot treat income earned by the (Pty) Ltd as exempt merely because shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 5 – Assessed Loss Brought Forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the assessed loss balance from prior years. The deduction of the assessed loss is subject to the 80% taxable-income set-off limitation for years of assessment ending on or after 1 January 2022.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred by a non-resident parent or offshore affiliate cannot be transferred into the South African (Pty) Ltd. The company must compute its loss on a separate-entity basis using arm's-length transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after deductions, section 11D R&D allowances, assessed-loss set-off, and any transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standalone taxable income of the South African company. Group consolidation is not recognised for South African income tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% corporate income tax rate to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the (Pty) Ltd is a South African tax resident, it is taxable on worldwide income. A non-resident company with South African receipts may be taxable through a representative taxpayer or an assessment at 27% on SA-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D, Box 8 – Rebates and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter provisional tax paid, dividend withholding tax and other credits, and any foreign tax credits eligible under a DTA or unilateral relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder's personal taxes are not rebates. Credits must belong to the South African company's own assessments; foreign taxes borne by the parent entity are not claimable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The resulting amount is either payable by the company or refundable by SARS. This is the final normal tax liability after all credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any dividends or royalties paid to non-resident beneficiaries must be reconciled separately in the applicable withholding tax returns, not set off in the company's final assessment unless they are statutory rebates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-submission triggers the Administrative Non-Compliance Penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act, a recurring monthly penalty scaled by taxpayer turnover and taxable income from ZAR 250 per month to ZAR 16,000 per month for large enterprises. The return further attracts interest at the prescribed rate and, where the assessment is understated, understatement penalties of up to 100% of the shortfall. Continued failure after SARS demand is a criminal tax offence with fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20.00% final dividend withholding tax on any dividend paid or credited to non-resident beneficial owners and, in prescribed circumstances, residents. The (Pty) Ltd is the withholding agent and must pay over the tax within one month after the dividend declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) confirm treaty residence in the relevant jurisdiction; (2) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign revenue authority, issued in English and valid for the year of payment; (3) provide the South African paying company with the completed SARS declaration of beneficial ownership and the TRC before the payment is made; and (4) where treaty relief is claimed after tax was withheld, lodge a refund application with SARS supported by the same evidence and the relevant DTA provision. If the documentation is not received before payment, the statutory rate must be withheld and the payer may otherwise be held liable for the tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for intellectual property, software licences, or game content attract a statutory withholding tax rate of 15.00%. Interest paid to non-residents similarly attracts a statutory rate of 15.00%, subject to exemptions for government interest and certain bank or listed debt. DTA rates usually range from 0% to 10% for interest and 0% to 10% for royalties depending on the jurisdiction and beneficial ownership; treaty shopping through shell companies is not recognised.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is generally required when the South African taxpayer's gross turnover exceeds ZAR 100 million, or when the aggregate value of cross-border connected-person transactions in a year exceeds ZAR 5 million. Master File and Country-by-Country reporting are required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding ZAR 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. Economic substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rules in sections 80A to 80L of the Income Tax Act, the substance-over-form doctrine, the place-of-effective-management residence test, controlled foreign company rules, and SARS's power to disregard arrangements lacking commercial substance. A South African (Pty) Ltd operating as a mere conduit without employees, premises, decision-making authority, or risk-bearing capacity will be recharacterised and its deductions denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting an ITR14 that understates gross receipts from Apple App Store and Google Play, inflates deductions, uses fabricated cross-border invoices, or conceals South African-source digital gaming revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under sections 234 and 235 of the Tax Administration Act, with fines up to ZAR 10 million and imprisonment up to 10 years; civil understatement penalties up to 100% of the tax shortfall plus prescribed-rate interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in or knowingly authorised the evasion can be joined in the assessment, subjected to asset preservation orders, placed on SARS departure prohibition lists, and prosecuted personally. The corporate veil is pierced where the company is used as a facade for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a shelf (Pty) Ltd with no employees, no office, no South African bank account, and no board autonomy; routing all MMORPG revenue to a non-resident shell while the South African entity accumulates only deductions and tax losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the company under the general anti-avoidance rules, tax the non-resident recipient as effectively managed in South Africa, apply CFC inclusion, or recharacterise the arrangement; the resulting additional assessment carries understatement penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors acting without substance are personally liable under section 77 of the Companies Act for reckless trading. SARS may attach personal assets, prohibit departure, and seek criminal penalties where the shell is used to defraud revenue.
